content.text:
I submitted **index 4 (Co 0.785 / Sb 0.215)** as the best composition, but all three EQE readings were effectively zero, so none of them looks like a real photoanode.

| Index | Co / Sb | EQE (%) | Why I measured it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | 0.32 / 0.68 | −0.0029 | Nearest to CoSb2O6, which the stability model (MACE) puts on the convex hull |
| 4 | 0.785 / 0.215 | +0.0022 | Nearest to Co7Sb2O12, 0.03 eV/atom above the hull, predicted band gap 1.44 eV (below the 2.4 eV light) |
| 8 | 0.68 / 0.32 | −0.0014 | Pick from the Gaussian-process suggestion tool, in the unmeasured stretch between 4 and 19 |

- **Choice of index 4:** it had the only positive reading. At these magnitudes that edge is probably not meaningful.
- **Middle of the library:** MACE puts CoSbO4 0.12 eV/atom above the hull. Films there are therefore likely a mix of the two phases above, not a new compound.
- **Band-gap predictions:** the tool gave 0.37 eV for CoSb2O6 and 0.83 eV for a Co5SbO8 spinel. Both look too low to trust for cobalt oxides, so I gave them little weight.
- **Not tested:** the ends of the line (index 0, most Co-rich, and index 29, most Sb-rich) and most intermediate points. If a better composition exists, it is among those.
- **XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phases actually formed is unconfirmed.
